note: The milestone sequence scripts/test-native-xnu-entry.py asserts in QEMU, written down as one list so a handset record can be judged against the same sequence. `symbol` is the kernel symbol the fixture breaks on and `fixture` is the milestone name it records, so the list is the single source for both. The transport that carries `marker` on real hardware is not chosen yet: a GOP framebuffer console written after ExitBootServices, or a reserved RAM mailbox read back by a diagnostic EFI application. Until it exists, P1.1 cannot be judged, because a successful entry and a hang both look like a black screen.

checkpoints.proves: DarwinBoot transferred control to the kernel image at its entry point, with the ADT boot arguments it built.
The kernel reached arm_vm_init, so the pmap and the early memory map are usable rather than merely parsed.
arm_vm_init returned: the VM structures were built without a fault.
The source corecrypto provider was entered after VM setup.
The provider returned and its POST ran; the fixture also reads its status word.
PE_init_iokit was entered: the platform expert is bringing up the driver tree.
The bootstrap thread started and reached kernel_bootstrap, after IOKit came up.

bsd_init was entered: the BSD subsystem is starting, which is the last checkpoint before a root volume is required. It needs the source pthread component registered (CONFIG_XNU_SOURCE_PTHREAD) or it panics on the first thread call.
